messages:
sec-bot: detection: scanner (gitrob + secret-scan) flagged a secret embedded in a public DockerHub image 'redwood/inference-worker:staging-latest'. suspected: API key with write scope. image pulled from dockerhub.com/rwinf/worker:staging-latest at 2026-03-30T09:05Z.

alex.m: thanks for the auto-alert. who pushed that image? any link to the digest or manifest?

sec-bot: pushed_by: ben_r. image_digest: sha256:4a7c...; layers mention `/app/config/.env` containing `REDWOOD_API_KEY=`. scanner excerpt: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_abc123...`

ben_r: omg — that was a local test image I pushed during a debugging session. I thought it was private. I didn't realize the repo was public.

maria.k: ok triage checklist: 1) mark token compromised 2) rotate immediately 3) revoke old token 4) search logs for usage 5) check customer impact 6) assess build/CI settings and RBAC.

alex.m: agree. ben, can you confirm the token ID if present? if not, we'll rotate all keys created around that time.

ben_r: the env had the full token string only, no token id. It was created by my user account ~48h ago for local experiments.

tess_cs: flagging customer-facing channels: if any customers saw anomalous behavior, we may need to notify. I'll standby for impact results.

maria.k: executing containment now. revoking token and creating new scoped key. running admin CLI revoke: `rwctl tokens revoke --token "sk_live_abc123..." --reason "exposed in public DockerHub image"`

deploy-bot: command executed by maria.k at 2026-03-30T09:12Z: result=success; revoked_token_id=tok_9d2f; propagation=global

alex.m: good. next: identify any service calls that used that token. ben, which environment did you use it against? staging or hosted?

ben_r: I used it against our staging cluster (redwood-staging) but I did try a couple of test calls against hosted API while investigating latency.

maria.k: pulling audit logs now. query: `audit.query --filter "api_key=sk_live_abc123" --from "2026-03-28T00:00Z" --to "2026-03-30T09:15Z"`

sec-bot: audit results: 7 requests found. IPs: 54.72.12.100, 18.205.34.9, 203.0.113.45; UA includes `curl/7.79` and `python-requests/2.28`. Two requests hit production model endpoint `v1/generate` at low rate, both unauthenticated? (they used the token).

alex.m: two production hits is concerning. check payloads and outputs — any data exfiltration of customer content?

maria.k: payloads show small test prompts, no customer-derived content. timestamps match ben's debugging times plus two extra distinct IPs making similar calls 3h after push. those look like opportunistic scrapers.

tess_cs: sounds like low impact on customer data, but token had write scope — could have triggered model writes or config changes?

maria.k: checked admin endpoints — no config writes or rollbacks. all admin calls failed with 403. token was a service key with text-gen scope only.

alex.m: we should still treat this as a P2 incident. next actions: rotate any other keys ben created, scan DockerHub org for other public images with secrets, update RBAC so service keys cannot have long-lived write scopes without approval, and add CI/DockerHub policy.

ben_r: I'm onboard. I already made the DockerHub repo private and removed the image tag. apologies.

maria.k: scanning DockerHub using our image-scanner: `image-scan --org rwinf --public-only --secrets` — running now.

sec-bot: scan results: 1 additional image had an env file but no tokens. only the staging-latest image had the exposed key.

alex.m: good. next: check if any third-party search engines indexed the image layers or env content. use `shodan`/public artifact search.

maria.k: did a quick public search (`github dork` and `artifacthub`). nothing else surfaced.

tess_cs: legal — do we need to notify customers or regulators?

legal: (joined) initial read: minimal customer data exposure and no successful admin operations. this is likely not a reportable breach, but we should document and follow our incident disclosure playbook. if the token had touched customer data, escalate.

alex.m: ok. action items and owners: 1) ben — rotate any remaining personal or dev keys and run `rwctl token list --owner ben_r` (due today). 2) maria — create short-lived service key template and push policy requiring KMS-backed keys for any long-lived tokens (due 48h). 3) eng-platform (ben + ben_r?) — add pre-push DockerHub scanner to CI and a CI blocker for pushing images with secrets (due 1 week). 4) infra (alex) — audit RBAC to prevent service keys with broad scopes; consider default min-scope (due 72h). 5) sec-team (maria) — produce incident memo and update runbook (due 24h). 6) legal/tess — prepare customer-facing FAQ if needed (standby).

ben_r: doing `rwctl token rotate --owner ben_r --confirm` now. will share outputs in #private-ops.

maria.k: adding temporary mitigation: enforce KMS-only creation for tokens with production scope. implementation note: KMS integration required role `service-token.kms_required=true` in token policy. pushing PR for console and API validation.

alex.m: also add audit log flagging for token creation without KMS binding. we want an alert for any future non-KMS tokens with production scopes.

sec-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-03-30-14 in our tracker. severity=P2. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-03-30-14

maria.k: quick follow: add mandatory secret scanning in PR pipelines and a post-merge job that scans built images before pushing to DockerHub. failing build should block publish.

ben_r: will run credential inventory script and remove leftover local copies.

tess_cs: I'll draft a short internal comms message for Customer Support in case customers ask.

legal: also note to preserve evidence (image digest, registry metadata, audit logs) for 90 days. will coordinate with infra.

alex.m: good. final: once the post-incident memo is ready, let's schedule a 30-minute readout with eng, infra, platform, and legal. thanks everyone — main thing is rotated/revoked and no customer data exfiltrated.

maria.k: closing loop: revoked token, no admin actions observed, limited production calls, DockerHub repo made private, CI/GitHub scanning PR opened, KMS policy PR opened.

ben_r: again, sorry — learned a lot.

sec-bot: incident status: containment=complete, investigation=ongoing (artifact search), remediation=PRs open, postmortem=scheduled.

alex.m: filing final checklist and moving to postmortem. thanks. :white_check_mark:
